title: Social Changes Under American Rule
subtitle: Schools, English, basketball, hospitals. Some of it you are still living inside.
objectives: Describe the public school system set up in 1901
Explain how English became a language of the Philippines
Describe changes in public health and in the position of the Church
Weigh benefits against costs without flattening either

cards.title: The change you can still see from your desk
cards.text: Act No. 74, passed in January 1901, created free primary schools across the islands. It is why school looks the way it does.

cards.title: What changed in daily life
cards.text: Tap each one. Every item here appears somewhere in the quiz.

cards.title: It was policy, not generosity
cards.text: The Americans believed a colony that could read English would be easier to govern and easier to trade with.
points: **Free primary education** for every child.
**Teachers were needed** in enormous numbers.
**Soldiers taught first**, before the teachers arrived.
**A real benefit** with a clear purpose behind it.

question.text: What did Act No. 74 of 1901 create?
options: A free public primary school system
question.explain: Free primary education across the islands. The largest and most lasting change of the period.

cards.title: The Thomasites
cards.text: About five hundred American teachers sailed to Manila on a ship called the USS Thomas. The name stuck to them.
points: **They were teachers**, not soldiers.
**They were sent to towns** all over the country.
**Many died** of disease within a few years.
**They trained Filipino teachers** who then taught.

cards.title: A group named after a boat
cards.text: Nobody chose the name Thomasites. It came from the ship, the way a nickname comes from something that happened once.
points: **The USS Thomas** carried the first big group.
**The name outlived the ship** by a century.
**Names in history stick by accident** all the time.
**Katipunan, Thomasite, Propaganda** — all borrowed.

options: American teachers who arrived in 1901 on the USS Thomas
American soldiers who fought at Tirad Pass
Filipino priests who left the Catholic Church
question.explain: About five hundred teachers, named after the ship that brought them.

cards.title: Halfway
cards.text: Part 2 is language, health, church and sport. Get a drink first.

cards.title: English replaced Spanish in the classroom
cards.text: Within a generation, the language of school, government and courts had changed. That decision reaches into your life directly.

cards.title: You are reading this because of 1901
cards.text: Filipino gamers play, stream and argue in English with almost no friction. That is a direct result of the school policy.
points: **English became the language of instruction.**
**It is still an official language today.**
**It opened work**, from call centres to shipping.
**It also pushed Spanish out** almost completely.

cards.title: Hospitals, vaccines, and a very bad year
cards.text: The Americans built hospitals, ran vaccination drives and set up sanitation systems. They also arrived with new diseases.
points: **Smallpox vaccination** reached most provinces.
**The cholera epidemic of 1902** killed tens of thousands.
**Quarantine was often enforced** by force.
**Health improved overall** across the period.

question.text: Public health under American rule improved steadily with no serious setbacks.
question.explain: False. Hospitals and vaccination helped, but the 1902 cholera epidemic killed tens of thousands.

cards.title: Separation of church and state
cards.text: Spanish friars had held land and political power for centuries. Under American rule they lost both.
points: **The friar lands were bought** and resold.
**Priests no longer ran local government.**
**The Philippine Independent Church** was founded in 1902.
**Aglipay led it.** It still exists today.

cards.title: Basketball arrived with the teachers
cards.text: American teachers and soldiers brought the game as school PE. It became the most popular sport in the country and stayed.
points: **Introduced through schools**, not through clubs.
**The Philippines has played it** for over a century.
**Boxing grew in the same period** through the US bases.
**Colonies leave sport behind** long after they leave.

cards.title: Both columns are real
cards.text: You do not have to choose between 'the Americans built schools' and 'the Americans took the country'. Both happened.
points: **Free schools reached millions.**
**The war before them killed far more.**
**A benefit does not cancel a cost.**
**Say both, in that order, and you are right.**

terms.def: The 1901 law creating free public primary schools.
About 500 American teachers who arrived in August 1901 on the USS Thomas.
The language school is taught in. It changed from Spanish to English.
Estates held by Spanish religious orders, bought and resold under American rule.
Founded in 1902 under Gregorio Aglipay. Also called the Aglipayan Church.

cards.title: The four that matter
points: **Act No. 74, 1901:** free public schools.
**Thomasites, August 1901**, named after their ship.
**English became the school language** and stayed.
**Benefits and costs are both real.** Hold both.

quiz.text: What did Act No. 74 of 1901 establish?
options: A free public primary school system
quiz.explain: Free primary education across the islands, and the most lasting change of the period.
quiz.objective: Describe the public school system set up in 1901

quiz.text: Why did the Americans prioritise schools?
options: They believed an English-reading colony would be easier to govern and trade with
Filipinos had never had schools before
Congress ordered it as a punishment
It was cheaper than any other policy
quiz.explain: It was a real benefit with a clear political purpose behind it. Both things are true.
quiz.objective: Describe the public school system set up in 1901

options: American teachers who arrived in August 1901
quiz.explain: About five hundred teachers, sent to towns across the country.

quiz.text: Where does the name Thomasite come from?
options: The USS Thomas, the ship that carried them
quiz.explain: The name came from the ship and outlived it by more than a century.

quiz.text: American soldiers taught in Philippine schools before the Thomasites arrived.
quiz.explain: True. Soldiers were the first teachers, until trained teachers could be brought over.

quiz.text: Which language replaced Spanish as the language of instruction?
quiz.explain: Within a generation the language of school, government and the courts had changed.
quiz.objective: Explain how English became a language of the Philippines

quiz.text: What is one lasting effect of the language policy?
options: English is still an official language of the Philippines
Spanish is still spoken by most Filipinos
Schools stopped teaching local languages entirely
quiz.explain: It also pushed Spanish out almost completely, which was not an accident.
quiz.objective: Explain how English became a language of the Philippines

quiz.text: What happened to public health under American rule?
options: It improved overall, but a cholera epidemic in 1902 killed tens of thousands
It got worse every single year
quiz.explain: Hospitals, sanitation and vaccination helped. The 1902 epidemic was still devastating.
quiz.objective: Describe changes in public health and in the position of the Church

quiz.text: What happened to the Spanish friars' land?
options: It was bought by the government and resold
It was given to the American army
quiz.explain: The friars lost their estates and their political role in local government.
quiz.objective: Describe changes in public health and in the position of the Church

quiz.text: What was founded in 1902 under Gregorio Aglipay?
quiz.explain: The Aglipayan Church, a Filipino church separate from Rome. It still exists.
quiz.objective: Describe changes in public health and in the position of the Church

quiz.text: How did basketball reach the Philippines?
options: American teachers and soldiers introduced it through schools
Spanish friars brought it in the 1800s
quiz.explain: It came in as school PE and became the most popular sport in the country.
quiz.objective: Weigh benefits against costs without flattening either

quiz.text: Because the Americans built schools, the costs of the colonial period cancel out.
quiz.explain: False. A benefit does not cancel a cost. Both are real and both belong in the answer.
quiz.objective: Weigh benefits against costs without flattening either

teacher.summary: Week 10 closes the Term 1 Social Studies arc with the social changes of American rule, matching the weekly scope. The hard part of this topic is not the facts, which are straightforward, but the judgement: the schools were a genuine and enormous benefit, and they followed a war with a civilian death toll in the hundreds of thousands. The lesson refuses to resolve that for him. The final idea card gives him an explicit sentence pattern — both, in that order — so that he has something to actually write in an exam rather than a mood. The language card ties the policy directly to his own daily life, which is the fastest way to make 1901 feel present.
discussion: Ask what changes in his own week if English had not become the school language.
Ask why a colonial government would want its subjects literate.
Ask him to name one benefit and one cost of the period and say both in one sentence.
Ask which of the six changes he thinks is most visible in the Philippines today.
teacher.extension: Have him find three things in his own day — a sport, a word, a school habit — that trace back to this period, and write one line on each. He should be able to defend the link.
misconceptions: 'Filipinos had no schools before 1901.' There were Spanish-era schools, but they were not free and not universal.
'The Thomasites were soldiers.' They were civilian teachers, named after the ship that carried them.
'American rule was purely beneficial.' The schools followed a war with an enormous civilian death toll.
'American rule was purely destructive.' The school system reached millions and still shapes the country.
